belief: People only like me for my money.
origins: Being asked for loans, gifts, or favors, watching friends change after a promotion or inheritance, or seeing someone use a relationship for gain can make it hard to trust anyone. Family conflict over money can also teach us that affection comes with strings. Some suspicion is wise, but when it turns into a rule that applies to everyone, it can leave a person lonely in a crowd.
teaches: Scripture is realistic that a crowd of companions can lead to ruin. It also says that a friend loves at all times and that there is a friend who stays closer than a brother. Samuel was told that people look at outward things, but the Lord looks at the heart. Jesus called His followers friends and laid down His life for them. These passages do not ask us to be naive. They invite us to look for love that is tested over time, to be a true friend ourselves, and to trust the One who loves us for who we are.
self_statements: If I had less, no one would be around.
I cannot tell who is sincere.
I am safer keeping people at a distance.
Nobody would choose me for me.
errors: Assuming I know that others are only after my money.
Turning a few painful experiences into a rule about everyone.
Feeling suspicious and therefore concluding that I am being used.
Dismissing real kindness as a trick.
questions: Which relationships have lasted through hard times, whether or not money was involved?
What specific evidence do I have about each person’s motives?
Have I ever been valued for something other than money?
What are the signs of a friend who is true?
How could I test trust slowly and wisely?
Am I treating good people as if they were the ones who hurt me?
truth: Some people have used me, and wisdom is not the same as fear. But not everyone is the same. God loves me for who I am, and there are people who love me for who I am too. I can use wise limits and still take small steps toward real friendship.
hw_truths: I am loved by God for who I am.
Wise boundaries are good; walls are not.
True friends show up over time.
I can be a true friend myself.
I can take small steps toward trust.
log: Each week, write the name of one person who has been kind without any link to money and what they did.
actions: List people who have been faithful.
Write down the names of people who stayed in hard seasons and what they did.
Decide ahead what you will and will not give, so you can be generous without resentment.
Take one small step toward a friend.
Invite someone for coffee or a walk with no agenda and notice how it goes.
Do one kind thing this week for someone without telling anyone.
prayer: Lord, You love me for who I am. Heal the places where I have been used. Give me wisdom to set good boundaries, courage to trust slowly, and the joy of being a true friend. Amen.
hw_questions: Who has stayed with me through hard times?
What evidence do I have about this person’s motives?
What boundary would help me feel safe?
What is one small step toward trust?
How can I be a true friend?
Where has old hurt shaped how I see people now?
name_example: Sarah can write: “A friend loves at all times, and I can look for and become that kind of friend.”
